Can't?  I would say no.  Given every deck was perfectly stacked, I would say that any combination of 3-5 heroes can beat any villain.  (Even Legacy, Parse, & Wraith vs the Ennead is winnable if Shu comes out last and you are very, very lucky)

 

That said, there are some combinations that require absurd amounts of luck.  The Play This! thread recently had trouble with AZ, AA, and Bunker vs Advanced Matriarch in Rook City.  I retain my belief that the game is solvable (although I haven't proved it yet), but you're unlikely to see a victory in a normal game.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
I 'beat' Advanced Ennead here with Legacy, Parse, and Wraith.  It's possible, although improbable.  And all other characters can deal non-projectile non-melee damage.  (Well, Setback can't except to himself, but he can redirect villain damage, which works just as well)

 

I just did the math for the AZ, AA, Bunker vs Matriarch matchup mentioned above, and it's easy.

 

Round one:
Horrid Cacophony x2, Impale, Syncophated Onslaught (Bunker & AZ), Flak Cannon [4], Toxic Sludge [5].  Matriarch at 61.

Round two:
Darken the Skies x2, ([3] from first Impale), Impale, Xu's Bell, (onslaught Bunker & AZ, [1]), Grenade Launcher (cannon [4]), Second Toxic Sludge [10].  Matriarch at 43.

Round three:

Carrion Fields x2, ([6] from Impales), Cold Snap, <some ongoing or equipment>, (onslaught Bunker & AZ, [1], Turret Mode [9], Dr. Tremane ([10] from sludge).  Matriarch at 17.

Round four: Darken the Skies, Hugin (destroy AA's extra card), [8] from AZ's start of turn, [1] from AA, [9] from Bunker.  Matriarch is at -1.


And I didn't even bother to try complicated shenanigans with AA.

Round four is the sweet spot for the Matriarch.  If you deal 70 damage to her before round 5, then (as demonstrated) you can basically ignore her deck.  Infinitor is probably going to be harder.

Well, Infinitor's strength is his shear damage output.  So low powered heroes are probably the weakest.  (Especially as since we're stacking the decks, deck control is rather useless in these scenarios.)  

 

The easiest way to deal with Infintor is to become immune to damage and then let Infinitor kill himself while you tank.  So an environment with a high amount of ongoing destruction may be the hardest to deal with.  But I'm not entirely sure.  And there's only so many heros that can pull off a full tank.  So if we're using non-tanking heroes, destruction might not be as bad.

posts.name: dclietz
posts.cooked:
I beat Advanced Infinitor with Parse, Fixer, and AZ in Rook City in 6 rounds, pretty handily. Infinitor was on his flip side after the first round and I'd specifically keep out one manifestation so he wouldn't flip back, and he only ever played manifestations. Rook City has 3 Statues, the scientist, and the detective so for 3 rounds it actually helps you and for 2 it is a non-factor. Parse's syntactic analysis is amazing when you can stack the deck and double targeting arrow off of snap decision is crazy. AZ did most of the damage since it is super easy to set up when you can stack the deck and play "risky" with his HP since you know what is going to happen. But even more powerful is 6 grease guns from Fixer due to Salvage Yard... which I realized after I started meant that the heroes would win very easily.

Going through the heroes, I think most of them would make a pretty big contribution against Advanced Infinitor and make the win easy enough in a stacked deck scenario. Many of the heroes can tank or otherwise mitigate a lot of the damage in different ways - Captain Cosmic (due to Cosmic Crest), Legacy, Nightmist, Scholar, Setback (wrong time and place), Omnitron-X (elemental exochassis), Naturalist, Haka (ground pound), Fanatic (Zealous Offense), Fixer, Tachyon (hypersonic assault), SkyScraper (monolith), Wraith (2x stun bolt), Visionary (2x twist the ether). Tempest can use Into The Stratesphere and Cleansing Downpour. The Sentinels have 52 HP (since there isn't a lot of all hero damage in the Manifestations) and some healing/tanking, and start with 4x unique capabilities. Unity would probably be OK due to recurring Stealth Bot.

That leaves Bunker, AA, Ra, Chrono Ranger, AZ, Expat, Knyfe, and Parse. My guess is that slow-build heroes (AA, AZ, Bunker) would struggle the most due to diffiulty controlling the initial wave of manifestations. But stacked deck AA is probably able to pull out pretty much anything. So maybe the team to try would be AZ, Bunker, and Knyfe?

Also - are there any worse environments for the heroes than Rook City? I'm thinking maybe Pike Industrial? The statues in Rook City are very helpful.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Wow.  I tried this a couple of times, and it is brutal.  I'm pretty sure that it is winnable, though.

 

Assuming all decks are stacked to make this winnable:

The simplest way to do it would be to bring out all the underbosses as fast as possible (Using Informants, Rook City is Mine, and Scum and Villany), and get the Chairman to reshuffle while all the Underbosses are in play.  Then Oblivion them all to hell, and let Nightmist sacrifice herself (doing as much damage as she can on the way).  Use Grease Guns to mitigate damage while the underbosses are in play.  When the deck reshuffles, put both Thieves on top.  One of DW Nightmist's incap abilities is to put the top card of a trash on top of that deck.  So, an Aimed Hairtrigger Reflexes, combined with that ability can completely lock down the Chairman.  While Expat is constantly Aiming, she's dropping guns for a finishing Unload, and Fixer is beating on his nemeses.  You're limited by the size of the environment deck, but you should have plenty of time to take down the Chairman and the Operative.  The only concern is the Operative damage from killing the thief over and over, and the Chairman's reaction damage, but those are both small enough that you should easily outpace them.
